name: Assembly Cost Estimator
blurb: assembly cost from unique parts, placements and extended-part fees
intro: A ballpark PCB assembly price from how many parts are placed, how many are unique, how many are 'extended' (not on the line's feeders), through-hole joints and fine-pitch parts. Two public fee structures are modelled: an online assembler that charges per solder joint and per extended part, and a contract manufacturer that charges per placement and BOM line.

inputs.label: Of which extended (non-stock)
inputs.help: Parts not kept loaded on the line; each costs a fee per order.

examples.title: Prototype run of 10 at an online assembler

usage: Give the number of boards, assembler type (econ, std or cm), SMT sides (one/two), unique parts and how many of them are extended, SMT placements per board and average pads per part, through-hole parts and pins each, BGA/fine-pitch parts per board, and optionally parts cost per board in USD and attrition in %. Returns assembly total and per board in USD, one-off vs recurring charges, a breakdown, the rates used and per-board cost against quantity. Use it to see what drives assembly cost (usually unique/extended parts at low volume, placements at high volume); it is ±50 %, not a quote.
sources: Rule of thumb: public PCBA fee schedules of online assemblers (per-joint, extended-part and setup fees, 2024-2025) and typical US/EU contract-manufacturer quotes (per placement, per BOM line, NRE)
